root_cause: rich 14.3.0 (PR #3930) replaced the width lookup in rich/cells.py with versioned unicode width tables. get_character_cell_size() returns 0 for any codepoint above the last range in the table (`if codepoint > table[-1][1]: return 0`), while unlisted codepoints inside the table range fall through the binary search to the default `return 1`. Nerd Font icons live in the Supplementary Private Use Area-A/B (U+F0000 and up, e.g. U+F024D, the downloads-folder icon), which is past the end of the table. So cell_len() measured them as 0 cells. That broke alignment in TUIs such as rovr; the issue reporter described it as the icons being counted as double width.
best_solution: In rich/cells.py get_character_cell_size, change the early exit for codepoints past the end of the width table from `return 0` to `return 1`. That makes it match the function's own default for unlisted codepoints (the `return 1` after the binary search): a codepoint the table does not list is one cell, whether it sits between two ranges or after the last one. Unassigned and private-use codepoints (Nerd Font glyphs, U+F0000..U+10FFFD) then take one cell, which is how terminals draw them. How to reason from the statement: the one clue is 'fonts' plus the issue link. The linked issue says Nerd Font glyph \U000f024d gets the wrong width after 14.3.0. CHANGELOG.md at the base commit shows that 14.3.0 reworked cells.cell_len and the unicode tables (#3930). Run `cell_len('\U000f024d')`: it returns 0. Reading get_character_cell_size then shows the out-of-range branch disagreeing with the fall-through default.
acceptable_alternatives: Any change that makes cell_len('\U000f024d') == 1 while keeping the other tests/test_cells.py cases (zero-width joiners, combining marks, variation selectors, wide CJK/emoji). For example, special-case the private-use planes (0xF0000-0x10FFFD, plus BMP 0xE000-0xF8FF) as width 1 before the table lookup, or remove the early exit and let the binary search fall through to the default 1. Editing HTML/SVG export font-family CSS does not work: it is the wrong subsystem.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_cells.py::test_nerd_font asserts `cell_len("\U000f024d") == 1` (a Supplementary Private Use Area-A codepoint used by Nerd Fonts, not allocated by Unicode). At the base commit it fails with `assert 0 == 1`. The existing test_cells.py tests (53) must keep passing.
locating_signals: The statement is only the PR title 'fix fonts' and 'Fixes https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/3943'. No file, function or symptom is named. The word 'fonts' actively misleads: it matches font-family strings in rich/_export_format.py, which is where the agents went. The real signals are only in the linked issue text (Nerd Font icon \U000f024d has the wrong width since v14.3.0) and in CHANGELOG.md at the base commit (the latest release, 14.3.0, reworked cells.cell_len and the unicode width tables in #3930). In a terminal-rendering library, 'font rendering broke after a release' means glyph cell-width measurement (rich/cells.py get_character_cell_size), not CSS fonts. The gold function is not named anywhere.
our_outcome_summary: Failed in all four configs (kaggle_env_pass false for v4, v6, v7, v8). v4 (197 s, 100 calls, hit the call cap) and v7 (366 s, 41 calls) produced empty patches. v6 (89 s, 22 calls) prepended 'Fira Code' to the font-family of the HTML export template in rich/_export_format.py. v8 (63 s, 22 calls) quoted "Fira Code" in the SVG export CSS in rich/_export_format.py and edited EXPECTED_SVG in tests/test_console.py to match. None touched rich/cells.py, so test_nerd_font still failed with `assert 0 == 1` (logs for v4, v6 and v8). Wrong location, because the agents read 'fonts' literally as CSS font-family strings without the linked issue text.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is only a terse PR title plus an issue link that you cannot open, do not grep for the title's literal word and patch the first hit. First recover the intent from what is in the repo. (1) Read the top of CHANGELOG/release notes at the base commit: a vague 'fix X' right after a release usually fixes a regression in code that release changed. (2) Read the title through the library's domain: 'fonts' in a terminal-rendering library means glyph width measurement, not CSS. (3) Look at the existing tests for the suspect module and write a small repro with an edge input (private-use, unassigned or out-of-table values) to find the branch that misbehaves. Inside a lookup or binary-search function, check that the out-of-range early exit returns the same default as the not-found fall-through: an inconsistent sentinel (0 vs 1, None vs default) is a common regression after a table or data rewrite. Never edit an existing expected-output fixture just to make your cosmetic change pass; that is a sign you are in the wrong subsystem.
